html:
The railway between Seoul and Busan, opened in 1905 and still the main rail line of South Korea. It runs about 440 kilometres down the length of the peninsula through Suwon, Daejeon and Daegu.

It was built by a Japanese-owned company between 1901 and 1904, as Japan tightened its hold on Korea. Japan wanted it to move troops and goods, and it carried supplies during the Russo-Japanese War. Korean land was taken and Korean labour forced for the work, which stirred anger.

The line joined Busan, the port facing Japan, to Seoul, and from 1906 another line ran on north to the Chinese border. With a ferry from Busan to Shimonoseki, it linked Japan to Manchuria by land. It was a backbone of Japanese colonial rule, which formally began in 1910.

After liberation and the Korean War, the line carried South Korea's fast industrial growth, together with the Gyeongbu Expressway beside it. Since 2004 high-speed KTX trains have run on the corridor.
sum: The railway between Seoul and Busan, opened in 1905 and still the main rail line of South Korea. It runs about 440 kilometres down the length of the peninsula through Suwon, Daejeon and Daegu.
